text:
Durchlauchtigster Fürst
Gnädigster Herr!
Ein seis 14 Tagen an alle hiesige Kammern erlaßener Befehl des
General Finanz Departements hemmt den Gang meiner Geschäfte
außerordentlich. und es kan lange dauern ehe ich mit Revision
der Taxen am Ziele komme, wann solche anders noch verstat¬
die Ursach dieser neuen Schwierigkeiten
tet wird.
ist der Prinz George mit den hiesigen Kriegs Rath Korn¬
Ersterer hat sich vor einiger Zeit bey der Kalischen Kammer
dem Korn als Revicor seiner Taxen über die in hiesigen, Posen
ſchen, und andern Departements belegenen Güter erbeten,
Die Kammer hatte dies auch accordirt. Da aber zum Unglück
die gerichtliche Faren, welche revidirt werden solten, von Korn selbst
gefertigt wären, und in dem Abord angefochten würden, so
müste dies dem Departements Chiff vorgelegt werden
betrüstet über diese Schwindelen, daß ein Mittglied der Kammer
die Taxen welche er selbst gemacht, und gegen denen man so viel
Ausstellungen macht, revidiren und die Kammer verantwortlich
machen solle, erlies der Minister den Befehl, daß

daß keiner Kammer, ohne Vorwißen des Gen. Finantz De¬
partements, mehr erlaubt sein solle Revionen einer
gerichtliche Taxe zu veranlaßen, wobey die revicion
der Prinz Georgischen Sachen sogleich für immer untersagt
würde.
Der Hl. Prasident v Goldbeck hat indes ſo
gleich an das p Departement geschrieben, und die Er¬
laubnis nachgesucht. Ich habe dies zu Estussette
nach Berlin gesandt, und zugleich Amelang und Langen¬
gebeten die Erlaubnis bewürken zu helfe und dafür
zu sorgen, daß selbige schleunigst hierher geschickt
würde. Es steht nun zu erwarten, ob der hämische Voss
die Revision nachgeben wird.
Ich muß indes hier vor Anker liegen und die Antwort abwar¬
ten. Unter des werde ich die Dismembrations Pläne zur
Approbation einreichen, und in dieser Sache alles ebene.
Der Hrr v Goldbeck war anfänglich sehr Lau, zuletzt
machte er mir Vorwürfe, daß ich ihm nicht zu den 2.
Strahlitz geholfen hätte die hernach Dolfs erhielt und die ihm
der Minister so vest zugesagt habe. Den Beweis daß
ich alles für ihm gethan, ward mir nicht schwer zu führen

und wir einigte uns wieder
Er wünscht sehr baldigst drey branzirte Büsten, die er
auf sein Repositorium sezzen will, zu haben. Des gleiches
hat er mich gebeten ihm baldigst ein Lavoir zu verschaffen
um sich seinen Kränkh unterleib täglich waschen zu können
Haben Ewr Durchlaucht doch die Gnade und laßen drey Büster
der Art, so wie auch ein Lavoir kaufen und schicken mir
dies mit erster Post hierher. Das Lavoir bekömt man
in die Tischler Magazine.
Ich mögte dem guten Mann gerne rechtschnell damit überaschun
Die Olesnicer Sache ist durch die freundschaftliche Vermittelung
des Herrn v. Husslarzewski an das Patrimonialgefricht
zum Entscheid zurück gesandt; dies ist für uns eine große
Satisfaction — Ich werde jezt die schnellste Betreibung der
Sache bewürken, und unter des Lichnowski beruhigen, um
Gebe nur der Himmel
mit Muße dis membriren zu können
daß ich die Erlaubnis zur Revision der Taxen baldigst erhalten
die verfluchte Schwindeleien des Pr Georg haben schon viel
Terreur gemacht, und werden noch viel Unglück und Mißtrau¬
erregen. Das ist doch ein schrecklicher Mensch – ich kan
Gott nicht genug preisen, daß ich mit dem Manne auseinander bei
In tiefster Hochachtung ersterbe
Ewr Hochfürstliche Durchlaucht
Wann ich nur bald die 3 franzirte Büſte und das Lavoir
erhalten könten es würde viel Freude machen.
Kalisz den 24ten Febr. 1805.
treu unterthäniger Diener v Triebenfeld

translation.en: Most Serene Prince, Most gracious Lord! An order of the General Finance Department, issued some 14 days ago to all the Chambers here, hampers the course of my business extraordinarily, and it may be long before I come to the end of the revision of the valuations, if indeed such is permitted at all. The cause of these new difficulties is Prince George together with the local Councillor of War Korn. The former some time ago requested of the Kalisch Chamber that Korn be appointed reviser of his valuations of the estates situated in this, in the Posen, and in other Departments. The Chamber had likewise granted this. But since, unhappily, the judicial valuations which were to be revised had been drawn up by Korn himself, and were contested in the [uncertain: Abord], the matter had to be laid before the Chief of the Department; and being incensed at these swindles — that a member of the Chamber should revise the valuations which he himself had made, and against which so many objections are raised, and should render the Chamber answerable — the Minister issued the order, that

that no Chamber should any longer be permitted, without the prior knowledge of the General Finance Department, to order the revision of a judicial valuation; whereby the revision of Prince George's affairs was at once forbidden for good. Herr President v. Goldbeck has meanwhile written straightway to the said Department and applied for permission. I have sent this by express courier to Berlin, and have at the same time asked Amelang and Langen to help procure the permission and to see that the same is dispatched here with all speed. It now remains to be seen whether the spiteful Voss will concede the revision. Meanwhile I must lie here at anchor and await the answer. In the interim I shall submit the dismemberment plans for approbation, and [uncertain: level] everything in this matter. Herr v. Goldbeck was at first very lukewarm; in the end he reproached me for not having helped him to the 2 Strahlitz, which Dolfs afterwards obtained, and which the Minister had so firmly promised him. It was not hard for me to furnish the proof that I had done everything for him

and we came to agreement again. He very much wishes to have, as soon as possible, three bronzed busts, which he means to set upon his repository. Likewise he has begged me to procure him as soon as possible a lavoir, so as to be able to wash his ailing lower body daily. Would Your Serene Highness have the goodness to have three busts of that kind bought, and a lavoir as well, and send me these here by the first post. The lavoir is to be had in the joiners' warehouses. I should dearly like to surprise the good man with them right quickly. The Olesnice affair has, through the friendly mediation of Herr v. Husslarzewski, been sent back to the patrimonial court for decision; this is for us a great satisfaction. — I shall now bring about the speediest prosecution of the matter, and meanwhile quiet Lichnowski, so as [text unclear] Heaven grant only that I may dismember at leisure, that I may obtain the permission for the revision of the valuations as soon as possible. The cursed swindles of Prince George have already caused much terror, and will yet excite much misfortune and mistrust. He is indeed a dreadful man — I cannot praise God enough that I am parted from the man. In deepest reverence I remain, until death, Your Most Serene Highness's — If only I might soon receive the 3 bronzed busts and the lavoir, it would give much joy. Kalisz, the 24th February 1805. faithful humble and obedient servant v Triebenfeld

Most Serene Prince, Most gracious Lord! An order of the General Finance Department, issued some 14 days ago to all the Chambers here, hampers the course of my business extraordinarily, and it may be long before I come to the end of the revision of the valuations, if indeed such is permitted at all. The cause of these new difficulties is Prince George together with the local Councillor of War Korn. The former some time ago requested of the Kalisch Chamber that Korn be appointed reviser of his valuations of the estates situated in this, in the Posen, and in other Departments. The Chamber had likewise granted this. But since, unhappily, the judicial valuations which were to be revised had been drawn up by Korn himself, and were contested in the [uncertain: Abord], the matter had to be laid before the Chief of the Department; and being incensed at these swindles — that a member of the Chamber should revise the valuations which he himself had made, and against which so many objections are raised, and should render the Chamber answerable — the Minister issued the order, that

that no Chamber should any longer be permitted, without the prior knowledge of the General Finance Department, to order the revision of a judicial valuation; whereby the revision of Prince George's affairs was at once forbidden for good. Herr President v. Goldbeck has meanwhile written straightway to the said Department and applied for permission. I have sent this by express courier to Berlin, and have at the same time asked Amelang and Langen to help procure the permission and to see that the same is dispatched here with all speed. It now remains to be seen whether the spiteful Voss will concede the revision. Meanwhile I must lie here at anchor and await the answer. In the interim I shall submit the dismemberment plans for approbation, and [uncertain: level] everything in this matter. Herr v. Goldbeck was at first very lukewarm; in the end he reproached me for not having helped him to the 2 Strahlitz, which Dolfs afterwards obtained, and which the Minister had so firmly promised him. It was not hard for me to furnish the proof that I had done everything for him

and we came to agreement again. He very much wishes to have, as soon as possible, three bronzed busts, which he means to set upon his repository. Likewise he has begged me to procure him as soon as possible a lavoir, so as to be able to wash his ailing lower body daily. Would Your Serene Highness have the goodness to have three busts of that kind bought, and a lavoir as well, and send me these here by the first post. The lavoir is to be had in the joiners' warehouses. I should dearly like to surprise the good man with them right quickly. The Olesnice affair has, through the friendly mediation of Herr v. Husslarzewski, been sent back to the patrimonial court for decision; this is for us a great satisfaction. — I shall now bring about the speediest prosecution of the matter, and meanwhile quiet Lichnowski, so as [text unclear] Heaven grant only that I may dismember at leisure, that I may obtain the permission for the revision of the valuations as soon as possible. The cursed swindles of Prince George have already caused much terror, and will yet excite much misfortune and mistrust. He is indeed a dreadful man — I cannot praise God enough that I am parted from the man. In deepest reverence I remain, until death, Your Most Serene Highness's — If only I might soon receive the 3 bronzed busts and the lavoir, it would give much joy. Kalisz, the 24th February 1805. faithful humble and obedient servant v Triebenfeld
summary_en: Reports that a General Finance Department order, provoked by Prince George's arrangement to have Councillor of War Korn revise valuations Korn himself had drawn up, now bars Chambers from ordering revision of judicial valuations without prior consent, halting Triebenfeld's work; President v. Goldbeck has applied for permission, forwarded by express courier with Amelang and Langen enlisted, though Voss may refuse. Meanwhile he will submit dismemberment plans, notes the Olesnice case returned to the patrimonial court through v. Husslarzewski, and twice begs for three bronzed busts and a lavoir for Goldbeck.
summary_de: Eine vor etwa 14 Tagen ergangene Verfügung des General-Finanz-Departements untersagt den Kammern, ohne dessen Vorwissen die Revision gerichtlicher Taxen anzuordnen, und hemmt die Geschäfte; Anlaß gaben Prinz George und Kriegsrath Korn, der seine eigenen Taxen revidieren sollte. Präsident v. Goldbeck hat um Erlaubnis nachgesucht, Amelang und Langen sollen in Berlin helfen; Minister Voss bleibt abzuwarten. Inzwischen werden Dismembrationspläne eingereicht. Die Olesnice-Sache ist durch v. Husslarzewski ans Patrimonialgericht zurückverwiesen. Erbeten: drei bronzierte Büsten und ein Lavoir für Goldbeck.
